film.language_id.desc: Identifier for the language in which the film is spoken

corrections: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows 5 values from 3 to 7 days, all well above zero, so the column is a ratio-scale number of days per film. The query shows how many films fall at each value. Evidence: SELECT rental_duration, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate FROM film GROUP BY rental_duration ORDER BY rental_duration -> [['3', '203', '2.8323645320197115'], ['4', '203', '2.97029556650247'], ['5', '191', '3.19942408376964'], ['6', '212', '2.895660377358497'], ['7', '191', '3.021413612565451']]

film.rental_rate.desc: Fee in USD charged each time the film is rented, covering one rental period of rental_duration days; it is a per-rental price, not a value of the copy.
corrections: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The profile shows rental_rate takes only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99, while replacement_cost runs from 9.99 to 29.99. The query shows how large and uniform the gap is. The auditor noted that the difference is always about −17 and the relative gap about −0.85, which fits two different quantities rather than one price seen two ways. Evidence: SELECT MIN(replacement_cost - rental_rate), MAX(replacement_cost - rental_rate), AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) FROM film -> [['5.0', '29.0', '0.16651517608314595']]

film.length.desc: Duration of the film in minutes
corrections: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified rating query already returns AVG(length) between 111.05 (G) and 120.44 (PG-13). The catalogue profile gives 140 distinct values from 46 to 185 minutes. So length is a continuous ratio-scale quantity whose group averages can be read directly. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(length) AS avg_minutes, MIN(length), MAX(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '120.4439461883408', '46', '185'], ['NC-17', '210', '113.22857142857143', '46', '184'], ['R', '195', '118.66153846153846', '49', '185'], ['PG', '194', '112.00515463917526', '46', '185'], ['G', '178', '111.0505617977528', '47', '185']]

film.replacement_cost.quantity: one-time asset value of a physical film copy (charged if lost or damaged)
corrections: quantity (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The column holds a per-copy value that becomes meaningful when summed over physical copies in inventory, for example as stock value. That is the reading of an asset value, not of a price charged per rental. Evidence: SELECT f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating -> [['G', '791', '16185.089999999853'], ['NC-17', '944', '19128.56000000009'], ['PG', '924', '17755.759999999962'], ['PG-13', '1018', '21052.82000000024'], ['R', '904', '18498.960000000006']]

semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns exactly 5 rating levels, each covering roughly 180-225 films, so every group is well populated and rating works as a grouping class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC -> [['PG-13', '223', '3.0348430493273613', '120.4439461883408', '20.402556053811544'], ['NC-17', '210', '2.970952380952388', '113.22857142857143', '20.137619047618937'], ['R', '195', '2.9387179487179553', '118.66153846153846', '20.23102564102554'], ['PG', '194', '3.051855670103099', '112.00515463917526', '18.959072164948356'], ['G', '178', '2.888876404494388', '111.0505617977528', '20.12483146067407']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows exactly 5 levels: G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17. These are the standard MPAA bands, which are ordered by audience restriction, so the column is an ordinal class. Evidence: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating -> [['G', '178'], ['NC-17', '210'], ['PG', '194'], ['PG-13', '223'], ['R', '195']]

film.special_features.desc: Comma-separated set of bonus features on the film (any combination of Trailers, Commentaries, Deleted Scenes, Behind the Scenes); the raw value is a combination, not a single feature
corrections: desc (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Returns 15 distinct values, all of them combinations of the same 4 feature names (for example 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes'). The column is a set, not a single category. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']] semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The verified result shows 15 distinct values, all combinations of the same 4 feature names, such as 'Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes' and 'Trailers,Commentaries'. The column is a set, not a single class, so it should not be offered as a grouping. Evidence: SELECT special_features, COUNT(*) FROM film GROUP BY special_features ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC -> [['Trailers,Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '79'], ['Trailers,Commentaries', '72'], ['Trailers,Behind the Scenes', '72'], ['Trailers', '72'], ['Deleted Scenes,Behind the Scenes', '71'], ['Commentaries,Behind the Scenes', '70']]
